A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same recursive LLM training study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching experiments relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original recursive fine-tuning experiments measuring quality, diversity and political lean, regression analyses, judge validation and supplementary sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds Wikipedia experiments, broader regressions, mixed-domain experiments and controlled toy simulations.

M1.justification: The accumulated-data chain, four base LLMs and LoRA procedure remain. Section 4.4 adds a procedural adaptation that combines three domains in training clusters and generates equal amounts of domain-specific content using three distinct instructions. This changes generation management without redesigning the base models.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from two Twitter and two Reddit datasets to include English Wikipedia paragraphs. Predictor analysis grows from webis_reddit alone to four datasets across three domains. Mixed-domain training and evaluation additionally test interactions between domains, extending the experimental scenarios beyond separate-domain chains.

E2.justification: Chen et al. (2023) remains the external judge comparator in v1 Table 1 and v3 Table 2. The four homogeneous-model chain comparisons are also retained. The new regression analyses and toy-model controls do not introduce competing methods evaluated against the proposed approach.

E3.justification: v1 analyzes 200 webis_reddit clusters using 14-predictor PLS with cross-validation and ridge regression with recursive feature elimination and AIC selection. v3 replaces this design with six-property regressions on 800 newly sampled clusters, dataset/ratio-specific fits and a pooled fit. It also introduces an 18-predictor mixed-domain design and controlled toy-simulation protocols.

E4.justification: v3 adds VIF feature-selection diagnostics, tests whether properties influence generation across domains, and investigates Wikipedia's nonmonotonic diversity pattern through a controlled histogram simulation. v1's vocabulary-size suppression analysis in Appendix B.3.3 is removed. Quality manipulation, model-count sensitivity and supplementary political-bias analyses remain, partly relocated.

E5.justification: Five-seed reporting and regression significance markers already appear in v1. v3 Appendix C.3 newly reports 50 simulations, and Figure 11 explicitly displays mean entropy with standard-deviation bands. This adds statistical reporting for the toy experiment without establishing increased replication of retained LLM experiments.

E6.justification: New multi-dataset coefficients replace the earlier PLS/ridge results; for example, v3 Table 1 reports pooled lexical-diversity coefficients of -0.0126 for relative semantic diversity and -0.0603 for relative quality. Mixed-domain analysis reports 21 significant effects, only three across domains. Wikipedia and toy-simulation outcomes are also added. These are new or revised results, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 introduces a simplified probabilistic model with a uniform integer distribution, normalized-histogram learners, recursive mixtures and a prior favoring multiples of two. Its bias and distribution-overlap assumptions add mathematical modeling content, although no theorem or analytical proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The main contribution expands from a webis_reddit-specific predictor analysis and Twitter-specific quality mitigation to property effects across several datasets, including quality and Gaussianity. The abstract, introduction and conclusion add the substantive claim that these effects are modular across domains. Dataset dependence and political-bias reduction, amplification and inversion remain central claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets weak cross-domain effects as supporting largely separate domain representations and independent shift dynamics. Appendix C.3 adds an explanation linking Wikipedia's intermediate-ratio losses to model priors and reduced effective training data. The explicit vocabulary-suppression interpretation is removed, while limitations concerning small models, English, US politics and chains without human intervention largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the withheld-code placeholder with a concrete anonymous repository link and adds Wikipedia provenance, filtering, sample counts and dataset-license information. It also documents predictor-selection decisions. Existing fine-tuning and hardware details remain, but the replacement regressions are less explicitly specified than v1's named estimators and tuning procedures.

R1.justification: The positioning around recursive training, model collapse and machine culture remains. v3 adds Schaeffer et al. (2025), Wikimedia and Völske et al. (2017), while removing references associated with PLS, ridge regression and Sentence-BERT. These are limited citation and positioning revisions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten around broader predictor evidence and domain interactions. Dataset details move to Appendix B.2, and the main-text quality-manipulation experiment moves to Appendix C.2. The appendix hierarchy is reorganized, alongside extensive wording, terminology and affiliation-number corrections.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the PLS/ridge displays with a regression table and mixed-domain figure, adds VIF and toy-simulation figures, redraws Figure 3 with Wikipedia and revised legends, and relocates retained plots. The visual organization changes substantially. Figure 4's new caption incorrectly reverses the beneficial/detrimental interpretation of coefficient signs relative to Table 1 and the surrounding text.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the evidence behind the central data-property claims: v1's predictor analysis relied on one Reddit dataset, whereas v3 uses newly sampled clusters across four datasets and explicitly tests effects during mixed-domain training. This addresses an important limit on the earlier findings' generality while retaining earlier validation and sensitivity checks. Wikipedia's nonmonotonic pattern and the controlled simulations also broaden the explanatory investigation. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, particularly the less explicit replacement-regression specification and the reversed interpretation in Figure 4's caption.
